2012_042_111312regmtg.paragraph: Agenda and supporting materials for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, November 13, 2012, 6:00 p.m., in the Services Building at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The consent agenda carried the October 2 and October 16, 2012 minutes and the September 2012 Treasurer's Report, which recorded total check disbursements of $2,345,929.96, ACH debits of $9,009.62, outgoing wires of $1,944,211.77 and total disbursements in the period of $4,299,151.35. Business items covered continuing summer tax collections beginning with 2013 and a Best Practices Incentive resolution certifying at least 7 of 8 criteria under Section 22f of the State School Aid Act for a $52 per pupil grant.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, regular meeting, Tuesday, November 13, 2012, 6:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (district office 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Agenda**
Recognition of Paula Fleming for 12 years of Board service (p. 4); consent agenda (p. 5) comprising the October 2, 2012 minutes (p. 6), the October 16, 2012 workshop minutes (p. 26) and the September 2012 Treasurer's Report (p. 27); 2013 Summer Tax Collections (p. 95); Best Practices Incentive Resolution (p. 97); change of the December 4, 2012 meeting start time to 5:45 p.m. (p. 100); closed session on attorney-client privilege (p. 101).

**October 2, 2012 minutes**
Called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart; Edmunds, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, Fleming absent; every vote recorded 6-0; adjourned 8:45 p.m. Resolutions honored more than 400 AP-exam students and the National Achievement and National Merit semifinalists (12-089), approved the consent agenda (12-090), issued probationary contracts to new hires Katie Lamansky and Cara Lebryk (12-091), named TEA/TESA/TESPA bargaining teams under chief spokesperson Jasen Witt for contracts expiring June 30, 2013 (12-092), seated the Sex Education Advisory Board (12-093), adopted the Storm Water Management Program Plan under NPDES General Permit MIS049000 (12-094), authorized study of refunding the 2004 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds dated August 12, 2004 (12-095), adopted committee assignments, certified MASB Delegate Assembly delegates for November 8, 2012 (12-096) and approved a closed session (12-097). The attached bond resolution authorizes 2012 Refunding Bonds not to exceed $47,000,000, with Stifel, Nicolaus & Company as underwriter, Clark Hill PLC as bond counsel and Stauder, Barch & Associates as financial advisor.

**Business items**
The Annual Summer Tax Resolution continues collection of one-half of school property taxes including debt service beginning with 2013, under 1976 P.A. 451, with collection expenses negotiated under MCLA 380.1612. The Best Practices Incentive resolution certifies at least 7 of 8 criteria under MCL 388.1622f for the $52 per pupil grant, due not later than June 1, 2013. The December 4, 2012 meeting moves to 5:45 p.m. to permit a closed session.

RECOGNITION. Paula Fleming completed her 12th year of service on the Troy Board of Education in June 2012; the recommended action is presentation of an engraved chair, citing student experiments at the International Space Station, national band and orchestra performances, and growth in NUMATS Midwest Talent Search winners, National Merit Semi-finalists and Advanced Placement participation.

OCTOBER 2, 2012 MINUTES. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with Edmunds, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present and Mrs. Fleming absent; Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Lesser, Machesky, Mull, Rajter and Witt attended with approximately 30 audience members. Student representatives were Asja (also printed Aja) Kepes of International Academy-East and Miranda Wilson of Niles Community High School. More than 400 Troy students were honored for AP exam performance across the College Board categories AP Scholar, AP Scholar with Honors, AP Scholar with Distinction and National AP Scholar; twelve juniors were recognized in person.

Resolution 12-089 honored National Achievement Scholarship Semifinalists Aaron Faison and Taylor Matthew and fifty-nine National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, who qualify by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT; a second WHEREAS block lists a separate roster honored as 2011-2012 semifinalists, signed the second day of October, 2012, with a reception set for November 7 at Athens High School. Resolution 12-090 approved the consent agenda (September 4, 2012 minutes, September 18, 2012 workshop minutes, August 2012 Treasurer's Report, non-renewal teacher contract); 12-091 approved 2012/2013 probationary contracts for new hires Katie Lamansky and Cara Lebryk; 12-092 named bargaining teams for TEA/MEA/NEA, TESA/MEA/NEA and TESPA/MEA/NEA, each contract expiring June 30, 2013, with Jasen Witt chief spokesperson and members drawn from Mark Rajter, Jan Keeling, Richard Machesky, Monica Papasian and Sara Konieczka; 12-093 seated the 2012-2013 Sex Education Advisory Board, co-chaired by Larry Hahn (principal, Baker Middle School) and Nicole Jenkins, with Mary McDermott (Troy High School), Kevin Wilson (Boulan Park Middle School), Rev. Jack Mannschreck of Big Beaver United Meth. Church, nurse Lois Winer of the Oakland Health Department and students Heather Turner (AHS 2014) and Dejan Jenkins (THS 2014); and 12-094 adopted the TSD Storm Water Management Program Plan under the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality Water Bureau, NPDES General Permit number MIS049000 and an Administrative Consent Agreement, covering projects disturbing more than 1 acre. Each vote was Yes 6, No 0, Fleming absent.

BOND REFUNDING. Resolution 12-095 recorded that the district may refund all or a portion of its 2004 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds. The attached Oakland County bond resolution authorizes 2012 Refunding Bonds not to exceed $47,000,000 to advance refund the Prior Bonds dated August 12, 2004 if sufficient present value savings exist, citing Act 451 of 1976, Act 34 of 2001, Act 354 of 1972 (MCL 129.131 to 129.135), Act 92 of 2005, Article IX Sections 6 and 16 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, Section 265 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267. Bonds carry denominations of $5,000 or whole multiples, mature on the first day of May, are held book-entry through Cede & Co. of the Depository Trust Company, and are secured by a tax levy without limitation as to rate or amount into a 2012 Refunding Bonds Debt Retirement Fund. Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated was appointed senior managing underwriter or placement agent, Clark Hill PLC bond counsel and Stauder, Barch & Associates, Inc. financial advisor; ratings may be sought from Moody's Investors Service, Fitch Ratings and Standard & Poor's Ratings Services. Todd Miletti, Secretary, certified adoption.

A second resolution numbered 12-095 adopted 2012/2013 committee memberships; 12-096 certified Paula Fleming, Todd Miletti, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the Michigan Association of School Boards 2012 Delegate Assembly on November 8, 2012; 12-097 approved a closed session under Public Act 267, Section 8(c), carried 6-0, with the Board in closed session from 8:25 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. and adjournment at 8:45 p.m. Superintendent Fowler's 2012/2013 goals covered college and career readiness, interventions for the lowest performing subgroups, preparation for a bond election in November 2013 including an external audit by TMP Architectural and Engineering Services, and the data processing system review.

OCTOBER 16, 2012 WORKSHOP. Convened at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building, all seven members present, with Teresa Pollock and Melissa Day of Plante & Moran Arch Environmental Group; agenda covered the district audit with Plante & Moran, a Teacher Evaluation Appraisal Model (TEAM) update, bond scope information from the TMP facility assessment study and a bond communications plan; adjourned 9:41 p.m.

BUSINESS ITEMS. Item 8.A: the Board intends to continue summer tax collections for the 2013-2014 fiscal year and to notify the City of Troy. The Annual Summer Tax Resolution, dated November 13, 2012, imposes a summer levy collecting one-half of school property taxes including debt service, beginning with 2013 and continuing until specifically revoked, pursuant to 1976 P.A. 451 as amended, forwarded to each city before January 1, 2013, with collection expenses billed under MCLA 380.1612; the certification paragraph as printed recites a regular meeting held November 13, 2013. Item 8.B: Section 22f of the State School Aid Act (MCL 388.1622f) provides $52 per pupil one-time grants to districts satisfying at least 7 of 8 best practices criteria not later than June 1, 2013, and the Board certifies being the designated policy holder for medical benefit plans, competitively bidding custodial, transportation and food services, accepting non-resident enrollment under Section 105 or 105c (MCL 388.1705), submitting a technology infrastructure plan for pupil academic growth assessments by 2014-2015, supporting postsecondary credit under MCL 388.511 to 388.524, MCL 388.1901 to 388.1913 and MCL 380.1471, offering online instruction, and linking the home page to MiSchool Data Portal dashboard indicators; it is filed with the State Aid and School Finance Office of the Michigan Department of Education. Item 10 moves the December 4, 2012 meeting start to 5:45 p.m. in the Services Building to permit a closed session, and item 11.A calls that closed session on an attorney-client privilege item under Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with roll call listing Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds and Fleming.
